topicName: Change Data Capture (CDC) Mechanisms (Log-based, Trigger-based, Timestamp-based)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Change Data Capture (CDC) Mechanisms: Log-based, Trigger-based, and Timestamp-based"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Change Data Capture (CDC) is a data integration pattern used to identify, track, and capture data that has been inserted, updated, or deleted in a source database. In modern ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, CDC replaces costly and inefficient full-table loads with incremental synchronization, reducing system load and data latency."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Trigger-Based CDC"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Trigger-based CDC relies on database triggers (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) defined on source tables. When a data modification occurs, the trigger executes a function that logs the change into an audit or shadow table."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Database-agnostic logic, easy to implement without specialized tools, captures exact row states."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Introduces significant overhead on transactional workloads (OLTP), adds lock contention, and consumes extra storage."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TRIGGER trg_employee_cdc AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON employees FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION log_employee_changes();"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Timestamp-Based CDC (Modified Data Tracking)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Timestamp-based CDC requires a column in the source table, such as updated_at or version, that automatically updates whenever a record is modified. The ETL process queries records where the timestamp is greater than the last extraction run."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Simple to query, requires no special database privileges, works well with existing schemas."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Completely misses hard deletes unless soft deletes are implemented, susceptible to race conditions during rapid updates, and relies on application-level or database-level timestamp generation accuracy."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"SELECT id, name, department, updated_at FROM employees WHERE updated_at > '2023-10-01 00:00:00';"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Log-Based CDC"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Log-based CDC reads the native transaction logs (e.g., PostgreSQL WAL, MySQL Binlog, Oracle Redo Logs) generated by the database engine. Tools like Debezium or Kafka Connect parse these logs to stream real-time events to the data warehouse or data lake."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Zero performance impact on source tables, captures inserts, updates, and hard deletes reliably, preserves exact transaction ordering."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Highly database-dependent, complex setup and maintenance, requires deep understanding of internal transaction log formats."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"name: postgres-connector
config:
  connector.class: io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector
  database.hostname: localhost
  database.port: 5432
  database.user: cdc_user
  database.dbname: enterprise_db
  table.include.list: public.employees"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary & Best Practices"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"When designing your ETL pipeline, choose log-based CDC whenever low latency and low source impact are priorities. Fall back to timestamp-based CDC for legacy systems where database logs are inaccessible, and avoid trigger-based CDC in high-throughput production environments due to locking and performance penalties."}]
